developments.title: kimi-k3 branch of DwarfStar adds K3.1 PRO inference from safetensors weights with SSD streaming
detail: The kimi-k3 branch of DwarfStar now supports K3.1 PRO inference directly from safetensors weights, utilizing SSD streaming architecture for model loading.
Inference performance is noted as slow but sufficient for quality assurance tasks, marking a functional upgrade for local AI workflows.
developments.why_it_matters: This allows QA teams to run K3.1 PRO inference on DwarfStar using native safetensors without conversion, streamlining local evaluation pipelines.

developments.title: DwarfStar adds SSD‑streamed DS4.1Flash support
detail: The latest update to DwarfStar enables the DS4.1Flash model to run via SSD streaming, delivering noticeably faster inference performance.
The change does not affect the earlier DS4.0Flash version, and a partial fix addresses a flaw specific to the 4.1 release.
developments.why_it_matters: Running DS4.1Flash through SSD streaming reduces latency for local AI workloads, allowing developers to execute the model more efficiently on consumer hardware.

developments.title: Addy Osmani publishes 'Your coding agents made you a manager' essay
detail: Addy Osmani has published an essay titled 'Your coding agents made you a manager,' arguing that developers who work heavily through coding agents have effectively taken on management responsibilities.

Its central line — 'Every gripe you have about bad managers is a bug report for interacting with agents' — reframes familiar complaints about bad management as concrete, fixable defects in how people interact with agents.
developments.why_it_matters: The reframing gives developers now directing coding agents a concrete way to act on friction today: each management-style complaint doubles as a specific bug report against existing agent workflows.
